```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

df = pl.read_csv('https://byuistats.github.io/M335/data/rcw_reshape.csv')

```



Key learning objectives: pivot and unpivot

Is data currently in long or wide format? LONG

Convert it to wide format:


```{python}
df_wide = df.pivot(on="Department", values="Count")
```


Convert it back to long format:

```{python}
df_long = df_wide.unpivot(index=["Year", "Semester", "Semester_Date"],
                            # on is the smooch or spread
                            variable_name="Department",
                            value_name="Count"
                         )
```


Explicit vs. implicit missing values.

Wide vs. long: when you want each?

# plotting


```{python}
(
    ggplot(
        data=df_long,
        mapping=aes(
            x="Semester_Date",
            y="Count",
            color="Department"
        )
    )
    + geom_line()
)
```




```{python}
df_zeros = df_long.fill_null(0)

(
    ggplot(
        data=df_zeros,
        mapping=aes(
            x="Semester_Date",
            y="Count",
            color="Department"
        )
    )
    + geom_line()
)
```


A little too busy with all the lines on te same plot, put it on small multiple:



```{python}
(
    ggplot(
        data=df_zeros,
        mapping=aes(
            x="Semester_Date",
            y="Count",
        )
    )
    + geom_line()
    + facet_wrap(facets="Department")
)
```


# Playing with names



```{python}
import polars.selectors as cs

df_zeros.with_columns(
    cs.starts_with("Semester")
      .name
      .map(lambda old_name: old_name.replace("Semester", "Sem"))
)
```
